title: Shift Letter Ranges Both Ways
statement:
You get a lowercase string s and a list of operations shifts. Each operation is [start, end, dir] and applies to every index from start to end, both inclusive.

If dir is 1, each letter in the range moves one step forward in the alphabet; if dir is 0, one step back. The alphabet wraps: forward from z is a, and back from a is z.

Apply all operations and return the final string.

examples.why: Net moves per index: +2, +1, 0. c→e, a→b, t stays.
Both ends wrap around: a back one is z, z forward one is a.
Overlapping ranges add up: the last letter moves −2 + 1 = −1.

hints: Applying every operation letter by letter can cost 50 000 × 50 000 steps. You only need the net shift at each index.
A range update "+v from start to end" can be recorded with two marks: +v at start and −v just after end.
Prefix-sum those marks to get the net shift at every index, then apply it once per letter with a modulo that stays non-negative.

explain.intuition:
The order of operations does not matter: each letter just moves by the sum of all shifts that cover it. So the question is how to add a value to a whole range cheaply.

A difference array does that. Write +v at start and −v at end + 1. A running sum from left to right then "turns on" the shift at start and "turns it off" after end. All the range updates cost O(1) each, and one prefix pass gives every net shift.
steps: For each [a, b, dir], let v = dir === 1 ? 1 : −1; do diff[a] += v and diff[b + 1] −= v.
Walk i from 0 to n − 1 with a running sum run += diff[i].
The new letter is ((s[i] − 'a' + run) mod 26 + 26) mod 26 converted back to a character.
pitfalls: Using % on a negative number in JavaScript gives a negative result. Add 26 and take the modulo again.
Putting the closing mark at end instead of end + 1, which leaves out the last index of each range.
Applying each operation to the string directly. That is O(n · m) and too slow at these sizes.

solutions.title: Apply each range directly
solutions.idea: Keep a net shift per index and add ±1 across every range.

solutions.title: Difference array
solutions.idea: Mark each range at its two ends, prefix-sum the marks, and shift each letter once.

followups: The operations arrive one at a time and you must print the string after each. What structure supports range add and point read?
Ranges are given on a 2D grid of letters. How does the difference array generalize?
